summary.verdict: On instrument characterisation this page is already past the five Best Hardware winners. Forty LEDs measured one by one, a 26% spread reported against parts sold as identical, and that measurement then killed the design it was meant to support, which is a move no winner page makes. Two things hold it back. The two sections that would answer the proof-of-concept question, Proof of Concept and Level Two Test, are headings with no data, while our own Digital Twin page carries a 24-hour culture run under this array that this page says does not exist. And the reproduction package stops short of a rebuild: the three PWM duty cycles that every intensity claim now rests on are nowhere on the page, the assembly guide section contains the words "Until it is written", and the bill of materials gives neither a part number nor a price for the LEDs the whole instrument is built around.
strengths: A measurement that changed a design, written in two lines. "Cycle 2 measured all 40 LEDs one by one and found a 26% spread across parts sold as identical", and the tiers then moved into the PWM duty cycle because matching alone left them 4 to 10% apart. Nothing in the winner set reports a finding and its consequence this tightly.

Status words with the mechanism in the same line. Measured, Partial, Built, Failed, Untested, Assumed, each with its reason beside it. No winner page labels a prototype as failed anywhere, and yours names the snapped post and the leaking holder in nine words.

Naming what a reading is not. The lux caveat sits in the opening and in 6.3, it gives the photopic peak, and it says the weighting error differs between the two channels. This is more careful than any caveat in the winner set.

The repair reported untested. "Neither change has been through a second overnight run on the shaker, so the repair is untested." That sentence is the hardest habit on a hardware page and the page has it in three places.

One part-numbering scheme across the exploded view, the section cut and the download list, with six STL meshes in stated units and in the instrument's own coordinates. Two of the five winners claim CAD files and link none.
priorities: Reconcile this page with the Digital Twin page before anything is frozen. Four notes below quote our own wiki contradicting this one, and the biggest is a whole experiment: the Digital Twin page reports a 19 September 2026 array run with six light arms, five time points to 24 hours and a logistic fit at R squared 0.997, where this page says "The biology run it was built for has not been done yet" and "no run under the LPA on record yet". That run is your answer to the proof-of-concept ballot question and it is sitting on the wrong page.

Put the three duty cycles and the three pin numbers on the page, and link the Arduino sketch. After 4.4 the whole intensity claim rests on software values that appear nowhere, and the pins are already legible in a photograph caption as P9, P10 and P11. Without them nobody can reproduce a tier, which is the heaviest of the four ballot questions.

Finish the assembly guide out of material already on the page. The hero gives the five parts in order, the section cut gives the stack and the 18 mm pitch, 5.4 gives the four screws and the heat-set inserts, and 5.1 gives the sliders. Number the steps against the photographs you already have.

Settle the wavelengths. The hero says 520 nm and 660 nm, 6.2 says around 535 nm and around 670 nm, and our Math Model and Photometer pages both use 535 nm and 672 nm. One page, two answers, and a third across the wiki.

Put one named person outside the hardware team in front of the instrument. Section 5.1's own goal is "an instrument someone else can use" and nobody outside the team is recorded as having touched it. Having someone assemble it from your own STLs answers the user-testing question and tests the documentation question in a single afternoon.

ballot.question: Does the hardware you developed address a need or problem in synthetic biology?
ballot.note: The instrument is derived from a stated experimental question before any hardware is described, which is the move the 2023 overgraduate winner was rewarded for.

ballot.question: Did the team conduct user testing and learn from user feedback?
ballot.note: Section 5.1's stated goal is an instrument someone else can use, and no person outside the hardware team is named anywhere on the page as having handled or assembled it.

ballot.question: Did the team demonstrate utility and functionality in their hardware proof of concept?
ballot.where: 04 Matched output, shielding and 05 Enclosed, set in code
ballot.note: Forty LED readings and a shaker run that broke the instrument are real functional evidence, but sections 07 and 08, which would carry the demonstration, are headings with no data, and the one culture run that exists is reported on the Digital Twin page instead.

ballot.question: Is the documentation of the hardware system sufficient to enable reproduction by other teams?
ballot.note: Six STLs in stated units and coordinates, print notes and checkable bore arithmetic, against a bill of materials with no part numbers or prices, no duty cycles, no assembly sequence, no code link, no lux meter model and no licence.

releaf: 04 DBTL Cycle 2: Matched Output and Light Shielding
05 DBTL Cycle 3: Enclosed and Software-Controlled Instrument
winners: Need: what the work requires and what cannot do it now
Overview of the device, often as a short property list
Design and build, by prototype or by subsystem
Demonstration: one run that shows the device does its job
skeleton.gap: Slots one, two, three and five are all present and slot three is stronger than any winner's, because three prototypes each carry a measurement that changed the next design. The demonstration slot is the hole: it is the one slot four of the five winners put last or second to last, and here it is two empty headings, so the page runs from a characterised instrument straight into its parts list. Our 02 Purpose also carries the need and the overview together, which works, and it leaves nothing to cut before the cycles begin.

extras: The summary gives one spread where you measured two. "found a 26% spread across parts sold as identical" is the green figure; 4.4 reports the red LEDs at 22%. Write "26% and 22%" or "up to 26%".
The research question asks about "protectant development". The rest of the page says protectant production or protectant expression. Use one term, and use the one the wet lab uses.
The summary stat reads "Footprint 211mm" where 6.2 gives "211 x 164 mm (217 mm across the sliders)". A reader sizing a shelf needs the second number. Give both, or label it as the long side.
"Level 2 Test: Intensity Variability" is the only use of a level scale on the page and there is no Level 1 anywhere on our wiki. Name the test instead, for example "Production against intensity".
Section 07 closes with "That relationship is the subject of section 8", and section 08 has no content, so the forward reference lands on an empty heading.

One fastening has four names: "connection point on the bottom plate" in 5.3, "connection posts" in Figure 13's caption, "a bottom-plate post" in the record block, and "cone-shaped posts" in Figure 9's description. Pick one.

Three of the six STL files are listed at exactly 196 KB (Bottom_Plate, LED_Holder, Tube_Holder). Check the sizes against the files before publishing; identical sizes for three different meshes usually means a placeholder.
Table 3's red columns are in kLux (0.390) where Table 2 read them in lux (390). The caption says kLux and never says the red values were converted. One clause fixes it.

"Full costing is kept in the LPA cost sheet, which feeds the cost analysis in the business plan." Neither the cost sheet nor the business plan appears anywhere else in our page set. Link them or drop the sentence.

The perf board is specified as "160 x 100 mm in the CAD" and Figure 14 marks it bought. One clause saying it is a standard 160 by 100 prototyping board would make it buyable, which is the only thing missing from that row.

Red at 670 nm here, 672 nm on both the Math Model and Photometer pages, and "about 670 nm" on the Bioreactor page against its brochure draft's 526 nm for green. Agree one pair of wavelengths across the wiki and cite Castillo-Hair for both.

notes.anchor: 520nmgreen channel
notes.title: Your hero and your spec sheet disagree
notes.body: This panel gives 520 nm and 660 nm. Your own Key Specifications in 6.2 say "Around 535 nm" and "Around 670 nm", and our Math Model page uses 535 nm and 672 nm for the same CcaS/CcaR switch. A judge who reads both ends of the page sees two different instruments. Pick the pair you believe and use it in all three places.
notes.after: 535nmgreen channel
notes.ballot: Is the documentation of the hardware system sufficient to enable reproduction by other teams?

notes.anchor: a green photon and a red photon mean opposite things
notes.title: The switch explained without jargon first
notes.body: You give the reader the mechanism in plain terms before naming CcaS/CcaR, so a judge who has never read an optogenetics paper still understands why the instrument needs two wavelengths. The last clause, that the instrument exists to hold that one variable still, is the purpose of the whole device in nine words.
notes.excerpt_note: Evry justifies a second device in one sentence from the first device's need. Same move: the requirement arrives before the hardware.

notes.anchor: Nothing goes into a culture and nothing is drawn out of it for the whole run
notes.title: Our Digital Twin page samples this run
notes.body: You write that nothing is drawn out of a culture for the whole run. Our Digital Twin page says of the array run that cultures were "read on a plate reader at five time points to 24 h", which means they left the array five times. One of the two accounts is wrong. Settle it with the Digital Twin team and write the same sentence on both pages.
notes.after: Each tube drops into the rack over an emitter that fires up through its floor. Nothing is added to a culture during a run, and the only thing that reaches it is light.
notes.ballot: Is the documentation of the hardware system sufficient to enable reproduction by other teams?

notes.anchor: A tube in a red column never sees green light from the column beside it
notes.title: Say which build this is true of
notes.body: This promises that no tube sees its neighbour's light. Your own overnight test found the opposite: "The white tube holder print allowed light to leak into neighbouring holes." The black four-loop holder is the answer, and 5.4 says it has not been through a second run. Name the holder here so the claim has a build attached to it.
notes.after: Every tube sits in its own bore over its own LED, and the housing closes the array in. The black holder is the version built to stop a tube seeing the column beside it.
notes.ballot: Did the team demonstrate utility and functionality in their hardware proof of concept?

notes.anchor: share a MOSFET and a single PWM pin
notes.title: A tier switches as a pair
notes.body: A reader who has only met the words six light conditions arrives at a design fact here and may not follow it. If a green and a red column share one PWM pin, there are three intensity settings on the whole array, and six columns driven by them. Say what that costs, which is that green and red at one tier cannot be set to different brightnesses.
notes.after: The green and the red column at one intensity share a MOSFET and a single PWM pin, so a tier switches as a pair. Three gates set the whole array, and green and red at one tier always run at the same duty cycle.
notes.ballot: Is the documentation of the hardware system sufficient to enable reproduction by other teams?

notes.anchor: Base plate, perf board, LED holder, housing, tube rack
notes.title: The same part under different names
notes.body: The fifth part here is a tube rack. Section 5 calls it the tube holder, the CAD calls it Tube_Holder, and the download list in 9.3 calls it Tube Insert. That list also renames LED_Holder to LPA Body and Bottom_Plate to Base Plate. Somebody downloading six files has to guess which is which, so use the CAD part names everywhere.
notes.after: Base plate, perf board, LED holder, housing, tube holder.
notes.ballot: Is the documentation of the hardware system sufficient to enable reproduction by other teams?

notes.anchor: A 24‑well LED array that holds engineered Bacillus subtilis WB800
notes.title: Wells, bores or test tubes
notes.body: A 24-well array reads as a microplate. Your own Dimensions fold says the instrument has 24 tube bores of 17 mm that take test tubes. Our Digital Twin page gives a third version, fitting its growth curve "on the plate-reader scale in a 150 µL well". Three descriptions of one vessel across two pages. Say test tubes here if test tubes are what it holds.
notes.after: A 24-tube LED array that holds engineered Bacillus subtilis WB800 under six defined light conditions at once.
notes.ballot: Is the documentation of the hardware system sufficient to enable reproduction by other teams?

notes.anchor: Cycle 2 measured all 40 LEDs one by one and found a 26% spread
notes.title: A measurement that changed the design
notes.body: Two lines carry the whole of cycle 2: what you measured, how many parts, what you found, and the design decision that followed. A judge reading only the summary already knows the tiers are set in software and why. None of the five Best Hardware winners states a finding and its consequence this tightly in an opening.
notes.excerpt_note: Evry kills its multiplexing plan with one number. Yours does the same to LED-selected tiers.

notes.anchor: The biology run it was built for has not been done yet
notes.title: Our Digital Twin page has this run
notes.body: You write that the biology run has not been done. Our Digital Twin page reports it: "On 19 September 2026, B. subtilis WB800 grew in light-programmable array wells under six light arms, read on a plate reader at five time points to 24 h", with a fitted growth rate of 0.299 per hour, R² 0.997, from the file lpa_growth_fit_20260919.json. That is your proof of concept, and this page says it does not exist.
notes.after: The instrument is built and characterised. One 24-hour growth run under the array is on record, from 19 September 2026 across all six light conditions; the production question it was built for is still open.
notes.excerpt_note: TUDarmstadt's culture test is one paragraph: volume, inoculum, strain, time, result. That is all this needs.
notes.ballot: Did the team demonstrate utility and functionality in their hardware proof of concept?

notes.anchor: every reading on this page is in lux, which is weighted for human vision
notes.title: Naming what the reading is not
notes.body: You say in the opening what the number on every chart is not, and why. This is more careful than anything in the five Best Hardware winners we read, and putting it here instead of in the limitations costs you nothing and buys trust for everything after it.
notes.excerpt_note: TUDarmstadt bounds its claim the same way: a functional microgravity environment, without eliminating gravity itself.

notes.anchor: Overnight run on a shaker Failed a bottom‑plate post snapped
notes.title: A failure with its mechanism beside it
notes.body: The status word is Failed and the cause sits in the same line, and the next row names the three fixes. None of the five winner pages labels a prototype as failed anywhere, and none puts the mechanism this close to the admission. Keep this block as it is.
notes.excerpt_note: Evry is the closest the winners come, and it takes a paragraph where your row takes a line.

notes.anchor: Culture run end to end Untested no run under the LPA on record yet
notes.title: Growth and production are not the same gap
notes.body: This row and the one below both say Untested, and only one of them is. A 24-hour growth run under the array sits on our Digital Twin page. What is still open is protectant production against intensity. Split the two so the growth run is reported with its date and the production question keeps the Untested label.
notes.after: - Culture run end to end Measured 24 h growth under six light conditions, 19 September 2026, reported on the Digital Twin page
notes.ballot: Did the team demonstrate utility and functionality in their hardware proof of concept?

notes.anchor: How does the wavelength and intensity of applied light affect protectant development
notes.title: The device derived from a stated question
notes.body: The question is in the reader's hands before any hardware is described, so nobody has to ask why a light array exists. This is the strongest opening move in the Best Hardware set, and Evry won an overgraduate award doing exactly this with an opsin protocol.
notes.excerpt_note: TUDarmstadt builds its need in four moves and ends on the gap in the prior art. Yours gets there in one question and does the same work.

notes.anchor: The strain carries a CcaS/CcaR light‑responsive expression system
notes.title: The switch is explained again here
notes.body: Your summary already says it: "The strain carries the CcaS/CcaR switch: green light induces protectant production and red light halts it. To measure that switch, cultures have to see a known wavelength at a known intensity with nothing else varying." These two sentences repeat that in different words, and the hero panel says it a third time. Keep the summary's version and start this paragraph at the requirement.
notes.after: To characterise that switch we need to expose cultures to defined wavelengths at defined intensities, repeatably, with nothing else varying. The LPA is the fixture that makes that possible.

notes.anchor: each channel is four internal‑resistance‑matched LEDs
notes.title: You matched output, not resistance
notes.body: You measured light output on a lux meter. 4.1 says you used those readings to identify units with similar internal resistance, which is something you inferred from the output. Resistance itself was never measured. Call the LEDs what your method made them.
notes.after: each channel is four LEDs matched on measured output
notes.ballot: Is the documentation of the hardware system sufficient to enable reproduction by other teams?

notes.anchor: under identical external conditions, which is the only way the comparison is fair
notes.title: Identical conditions are not on record
notes.body: Our Digital Twin page says of the array run that "The LPA run's temperature was not recorded." So identical external conditions are a design intention here, not a logged fact. The second half of the sentence also claims too much, because a sequential run with a temperature log would be a fair comparison too. Claim the design and leave the record to the run.
notes.after: One run therefore compares low, medium and high intensity at both wavelengths at the same time, in the same incubator and the same medium, so nothing outside the light differs between conditions.
notes.ballot: Did the team demonstrate utility and functionality in their hardware proof of concept?

notes.anchor: Intensity is set by pulse‑width modulation from an Arduino through three MOSFETs
notes.title: The drive chain is stated again
notes.body: This sentence, 5.2's build paragraph, Figure 8's caption and the Control row in 6.2 all say that an Arduino drives three MOSFETs, one per tier, held constant for a test. Four statements of one fact. Keep it where the build is described, and leave Purpose with the consequence only.
notes.after: Intensity is set in software before a run and held for the whole of it. The LPA applies a fixed dose and does not adjust output as it goes. It characterises, it does not control.

notes.anchor: LLearnLED output varies, and outside light gets in
notes.title: A learn with no test behind it
notes.body: Your section numbers run 3.1, 3.2, then 3.4, and this strip has D, B and L with no T. So a reader cannot tell whether the two faults below were measured or noticed, and the 26% spread was in fact measured in cycle 2. One line saying how you found each fault closes the gap, and the honest answer may be that you saw them.
notes.after:
- TTest[how the two faults below were found: by eye under room light, or on the meter]
- LLearnLED output varies, and outside light gets in
notes.ballot: Did the team demonstrate utility and functionality in their hardware proof of concept?

notes.anchor: Nominally identical cheap single‑bulb LEDs draw different currents
notes.title: Cheap is not a specification
notes.body: Cheap and single-bulb do not tell a reader what to buy, and both LED rows in your bill of materials are blank. This is the one component the whole instrument is built around. Put the package and the drive condition into the sentence.
notes.after: Nominally identical [5 mm through-hole] LEDs draw different currents and emit different intensities at the same drive level.
notes.ballot: Is the documentation of the hardware system sufficient to enable reproduction by other teams?

notes.anchor: the column can be recalibrated as a unit through straightforward mathematical adjustment
notes.title: Name the adjustment or drop it
notes.body: Straightforward mathematical adjustment is not a method a reader can repeat, and 4.4 then overturns the idea: matching alone left the tiers 4 to 10% apart, so the tiers moved into the PWM duty cycle. Write this as the plan you held before the readings came in, so the reader is not carrying a method the next section discards.
notes.after: The plan was to recalibrate each column as a unit, so that every column at a given tier matched every other. 4.4 shows why that was not enough.
notes.ballot: Is the documentation of the hardware system sufficient to enable reproduction by other teams?

notes.anchor: Coverage was added to block external light
notes.title: Say what the coverage was
notes.body: Coverage could be card, foil, a printed lid or a dark room. The housing does not arrive until cycle 3, so a reader rebuilding cycle 2 has nothing to make from this. One clause saying what you put over the array is enough.
notes.ballot: Is the documentation of the hardware system sufficient to enable reproduction by other teams?

notes.anchor: so each reading is taken at the same distance and orientation
notes.title: The condition that makes the readings comparable
notes.body: Forty readings only mean something if they were taken the same way, and you fix the distance, the orientation and the drive voltage in one clause before a single number appears. The row and column tag in the next sentence then ties every reading to a physical part. These two moves are what let a judge believe the 26% figure.
notes.excerpt_note: UBC fixes a standard depth before quoting the voltage and current, for exactly this reason.

notes.anchor: The array was then rewired with the matched units grouped into columns
notes.title: Publish the map from tag to column
notes.body: The readings are labelled A to D and 1 to 5, and you say clearly that this is not the array's 4 by 6 grid. What is missing is the mapping between the two. Without it a reader cannot tell which measured LED ended up in which column, so the tables cannot be checked against the instrument.
notes.ballot: Is the documentation of the hardware system sufficient to enable reproduction by other teams?

notes.anchor: All 20 green LEDs were read in kLux and all 20 red LEDs in lux
notes.title: The green and red scales differ
notes.body: Green is read in kLux and red in lux, and Table 3 then quietly converts red to kLux. A reader doing arithmetic across the two tables will be out by a factor of a thousand. Say why the scales differ and give one unit in the prose.
notes.after: All 40 LEDs were read at 5 V on the same meter. Green is reported in kLux and red in lux, because [the meter changes range between them]; Table 3 puts both in kLux.

notes.anchor: so the matching step is not optional
notes.title: This conclusion was already drawn
notes.body: Cycle 1's Learn says it: "As long as that is true, an intensity tier is not a real quantity." Repeating the judgement after the measurement weakens the measurement, which speaks for itself. The two sentences before this one already carry the finding.
notes.after: The green LEDs ran from 2.01 to 2.54 kLux, a spread of 26% across parts sold as identical. The red LEDs ran from 360 to 438 lux, a spread of 22%.

notes.anchor: The green low group holds 2.33 to 2.34
notes.title: The group spreads are given again
notes.body: The stat block above this paragraph already gives 0.4%, 0.9% and 1.7% for green and 1.8%, 1.5% and 1.7% for red, and Table 3 lists every value behind them. This sentence is a third telling. Your editor's rule is to keep one when the prose and the block say the same thing.
notes.after: Sorting by measured output tightens each group considerably, as the figures above this paragraph show.

notes.anchor: It is the leftover group, made of what did not match anything else
notes.title: You name your own weakest group
notes.body: You report the loosest of the three green groups, give its spread against the other two, and explain why it is loose, which is that it holds what was left after the others were formed. A judge does not have to find this, because you found it. Graded admissions like this are the thing the winners do least well.
notes.excerpt_note: Aachen grades its worse result instead of dropping it: less optimal, slightly lower sensitivity, still usable.

notes.anchor: they are not three distinct light levels
notes.title: The measurement kills the design
notes.body: This is the best piece of reasoning on the page. You give the two gaps, say where they come from, and conclude that what you built is not what you thought you had built. The sentence after it moves the tiers into software. A failure with its mechanism and its answer, in three lines.
notes.excerpt_note: Evry's one sentence of physics does the same job: only one LED lit at a time, so each runs at a ninety-sixth of its intensity.

notes.anchor: Turn the array into an instrument someone else can use
notes.title: Nobody outside the team has used it
notes.body: This section's stated goal is an instrument someone else can use, and the page never names anyone outside the hardware team who has handled it. That is ballot question two, and no Best Hardware winner we read answers it well either, so one afternoon would put you ahead of all five. Ask someone from another subteam to assemble the array from your STLs and write down where they got stuck.
notes.excerpt_note: TUDarmstadt names two outside researchers and lists four limits they identified. The whole move fits in a paragraph.
notes.ballot: Did the team conduct user testing and learn from user feedback?

notes.anchor: Cycle 3 keeps the calibrated tiers and the light shielding from cycle 2
notes.title: The section summarises itself again
notes.body: The line above this section already says it: "Turn the array into an instrument someone else can use: enclosed, set in code, assembled without tools, with the tubes held at a fixed distance over the LEDs." This sentence repeats that in more words. Start 5.1 at the four changes.
notes.after: Four changes turn the array into something that can be handed to someone else and used. Each is tagged with the CAD part it lives in.

notes.anchor: Slider prints allow assembly and disassembly without tools
notes.title: The assembly is not tool free
notes.body: Sliders mean the housing opens without tools. But 5.4 puts four screws through the bottom plate, the bill of materials lists screws and heat-set inserts, and heat-set inserts need an iron. Say which joints are tool free, because a reader building this needs to know what to have on the bench.
notes.after: Slider prints let the housing be opened and closed without tools. The bottom plate still takes four screws into heat-set inserts.
notes.ballot: Is the documentation of the hardware system sufficient to enable reproduction by other teams?

notes.anchor: software sets the duty cycle for each tier
notes.title: The duty cycles are not on the page
notes.body: Every intensity claim now rests on three duty cycles, and those three numbers appear nowhere. The pin numbers are in a photograph caption as P9, P10 and P11, so they are known too. Add one line with the pins and the duty cycles, and link or print the Arduino sketch, which is the only item in 5.1 the page never gives a file for.
notes.after: Control runs from an Arduino Uno R4 WiFi. Pins [P9, P10, P11] drive three MOSFETs, one per intensity tier, at duty cycles of [low], [mid] and [high] per cent. The sketch is at [link].
notes.excerpt_note: Evry shows the arithmetic behind its power rails so a reader can check it. Cornell names the deliverable another team needs and itemises what is in it.
notes.ballot: Is the documentation of the hardware system sufficient to enable reproduction by other teams?

notes.anchor: Three calibrated tiers across two wavelengths give six defined light conditions per run
notes.title: Calibrated against what
notes.body: Calibrated is doing work it has not earned. 4.4 found the LED-matched tiers were not three distinct levels, and the tiers now come from duty cycles the page does not state. A reader meets the word and assumes a reference instrument. Say matched and set in software, which is what you did.
notes.after: Three software-set tiers across two wavelengths give six light conditions per run, with the four LEDs in each column matched on measured output.
notes.ballot: Is the documentation of the hardware system sufficient to enable reproduction by other teams?

notes.anchor: Nothing in the light path changes during a run
notes.title: The caption repeats the paragraph
notes.body: 5.2 already says it: "The selected intensities are held constant for the duration of a test, so each culture receives a fixed, well-defined dose." The caption says it again almost word for word. Your editor's rule is to keep one. Let the caption carry what the figure shows and the paragraph cannot.
notes.after: Figure 8 Drive chain One Arduino pin and one MOSFET per tier, each switching a green and a red column of four.

notes.anchor: the frequency was most likely too high for the printed post
notes.title: Give the shaker speed
notes.body: Most likely too high is a guess, and a reader cannot weigh it without the number. Your own Figure 12 caption describes the shaker's dial, so the speed is in your hands. State it, and keep the guess marked as a guess.
notes.after: The LPA was on a shaker at [rpm] for the run. The post most likely failed at that speed, although we have not run it slower to check.
notes.ballot: Did the team demonstrate utility and functionality in their hardware proof of concept?

notes.anchor: This compromised our data, as the test tubes were receiving light from more than one source
notes.title: There is no data on this page
notes.body: You say the leak compromised our data, and your own record block says no run under the array is on record. A reader cannot tell what was compromised. Either name the run and what was in the tubes, or say the leak was found before any readings were taken.
notes.after: The white tube holder print let light leak into neighbouring bores, so a tube could receive light from more than one column. [What was in the tubes, and what the leak cost.]
notes.ballot: Did the team demonstrate utility and functionality in their hardware proof of concept?

notes.anchor: Neither change has been through a second overnight run on the shaker
notes.title: The fix and its untested status together
notes.body: You give the change, the reason it works, and the fact that it has not been through a second overnight run, in one short paragraph. Naming what has not been tested yet is the hardest habit on a hardware page and you have it. A judge trusts the rest of the page more because of this sentence.
notes.excerpt_note: TUDarmstadt describes its OD sensor in part-level detail and reports it neither tested nor integrated, in the same paragraph.

notes.anchor: increased its wall thickness from 2 loops to 4
notes.title: Loops is a slicer word
notes.body: Wall loops is slicer vocabulary, so give the wall in millimetres as well. The paragraph also leaves out why the change works, and you already know: your Dimensions fold says there is only 1 mm of PLA between neighbouring bores, and white PLA passes light through 1 mm where black does not.
notes.after: We replaced the white tube holder with a black one and raised its walls from 2 loops to 4, about [mm] of PLA. White PLA passes light through the 1 mm wall between bores; black does not.
notes.ballot: Is the documentation of the hardware system sufficient to enable reproduction by other teams?

notes.anchor: The final CAD is rendered in 3D at the top of this page
notes.title: A contents list the captions already carry
notes.body: This sentence tells the reader what each of the next four figures will be, and then those figures arrive with captions saying the same. Fifty words the page does not need. Keep the one fact a caption cannot carry, which is that the render at the top is the final build.
notes.after: The 3D render at the top of this page is the final build, with the black tube holder of 5.4.

notes.anchor: Around 535 nm, which induces protectant expression
notes.title: Put the dose the cells need beside it
notes.body: You give what the instrument emits and never what the switch needs. The number is on your own page, at the very bottom: a half-maximal point of 4.66 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹. Put it next to the channel so a judge can see whether the tiers reach it, and say plainly that your readings are not yet in those units.
notes.after: Green channel Around 535 nm, which induces protectant expression. The switch is half maximal at 4.66 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹; our tiers are in lux and not yet converted.
notes.excerpt_note: Cornell puts capability and requirement in one sentence: 37 klux available against the 3,000 lux the organism needs.
notes.ballot: Did the team demonstrate utility and functionality in their hardware proof of concept?

notes.anchor: Three, resistance‑matched and mathematically recalibrated to match across columns
notes.title: The spec sheet keeps a method you dropped
notes.body: This row says the tiers are resistance-matched and mathematically recalibrated. 4.4 says the opposite: "The tiers therefore have to come from the PWM duty cycle, not from LED selection", because matching alone left them 4 to 10% apart. A judge reading your specification gets the design you abandoned.
notes.after: Intensity tiers Three, set by PWM duty cycle, with the four LEDs in each column matched on measured output (4.4)
notes.ballot: Is the documentation of the hardware system sufficient to enable reproduction by other teams?

notes.anchor: External‑light coverage isolating the cultures from ambient light
notes.title: Isolating is stronger than you can show
notes.body: Isolating the cultures from ambient light is an absolute claim, and the page never measures how much ambient light the coverage keeps out. The overnight run also showed light crossing between bores inside the instrument. Describe the part here and leave the performance to the section that tested it.
notes.after: Shielding A printed cover over the array, so ambient light does not reach the tubes. Not yet measured with the room lights on and off.

notes.anchor: Tall print sized to hold test tubes at a fixed distance from the array
notes.title: Give the distance from LED to tube
notes.body: A fixed distance is the one optical dimension that sets the dose, and the page never gives it. Your Dimensions fold already has the tube holder's 80 mm height and the 3 mm lip, so the number is in the CAD. State it here, because without it nobody can reproduce an intensity.
notes.ballot: Is the documentation of the hardware system sufficient to enable reproduction by other teams?

notes.anchor: the 18 mm pitch less a 17 mm bore
notes.title: Arithmetic a reader can check
notes.body: You give the pitch, the bore and the subtraction, so a reader can verify the 1 mm wall without opening a file, and the fold says its numbers come from the CAD and not from calipers. That 1 mm is also the mechanism behind your light leak, which makes this the most useful line in the fold.
notes.excerpt_note: Evry's power budget works the same way: every multiplication is shown, so the claim can be checked.

notes.anchor: The LPA applies a fixed dose and does not respond to the culture
notes.title: Purpose already made this point
notes.body: Purpose says it in six words: "It characterises, it does not control." The first clause here repeats that. What is new is the consequence for the bioreactor, so keep that and let the earlier sentence stand.
notes.after: Nothing here transfers directly to the bioreactor without a feedback path being added. That is deliberate.

notes.anchor: so the stated peaks are assumptions until the LEDs are characterised
notes.title: The central claim labelled an assumption
notes.body: The wavelengths are the instrument's whole point, and you say they have never been measured on your own parts. Evry won an overgraduate award with the same gap and never admitted it, since its illuminator was never measured by the lux sensor built to measure it. Yours says so on the page, and that is the difference between a gap and a hidden one.
notes.excerpt_note: Evry opens by making documentation a design constraint and then leaves its own light unmeasured. Saying so, as you do, is what that page lacks.

notes.anchor: so the weighting error is not the same size on the green and the red channel
notes.title: Say which channel the lux figure understates
notes.body: You name the problem and stop there, so a reader still compares 2.33 kLux of green with 0.40 kLux of red as though the gap were real. The direction is known from the curve you just cited. Cycle 1 raised the green against red comparison as a fairness problem, and this is the sentence that can close it.
notes.after: Lux is weighted for human vision, which peaks near 555 nm. That weighting is near its maximum on the green channel and far down the curve on the red, so the red readings understate photon flux by more than the green ones do. Until both are converted, the green and the red tiers cannot be compared with each other.
notes.ballot: Did the team demonstrate utility and functionality in their hardware proof of concept?

notes.anchor: The purpose of this section is to show a culture run completed end to end under the LPA
notes.title: This section's run is on another page
notes.body: The section says what it would show and shows nothing. Our Digital Twin page has the run: 19 September 2026, six light arms, five time points to 24 hours, a logistic fit at R² 0.997. Bring it here as one paragraph with the strain, the medium, the volume, the n and the times, then say what it does not show. That answers ballot question three, which is your weakest.
notes.after: On [19 September 2026] we ran [strain] in [medium] under all six light conditions for 24 hours, sampling at five time points. [What the run showed.] It does not yet show any relationship between intensity and production rate, which is the subject of section 8.
notes.excerpt_note: One paragraph, with volume, inoculum, strain, time and the observation that settles it. Then straight back to hardware.
notes.ballot: Did the team demonstrate utility and functionality in their hardware proof of concept?

notes.anchor: This is the test the LPA was built for
notes.title: A heading, a question and nothing else
notes.body: The section states the experiment and stops, so a judge meets an empty section where the page's main claim belongs. Your record block already has the honest words for it: "the question the array was built to answer is still open". Put them here, with what is ready and what is not.
notes.after: This is the test the LPA was built for. Holding wavelength fixed and varying intensity across the three tiers, does protectant production change with the intensity applied? The instrument is ready and the run has not been done. [What is still needed before it can be.]
notes.ballot: Did the team demonstrate utility and functionality in their hardware proof of concept?

notes.anchor: Full costing is kept in the LPA cost sheet
notes.title: Full costing both exists and does not
notes.body: This says full costing is kept in a cost sheet. The fold just below says "Unit costs and suppliers are not on record yet", and every cost cell in the table is empty. Neither the cost sheet nor the business plan is linked, or named anywhere else on our wiki. Promising a file and not linking it is the commonest reproduction failure in the Best Hardware winners, so a judge will see it.
notes.after: Unit costs and suppliers are not on record yet. [Link the LPA cost sheet here once it is filled in.]
notes.ballot: Is the documentation of the hardware system sufficient to enable reproduction by other teams?

notes.anchor: Twelve LEDs of each colour go into the array, picked from twenty of each
notes.title: The table's scope set before the numbers
notes.body: Three sentences tell a reader what this table counts, what it shares with other instruments and what is missing, before a single cell. A reader knows exactly what they are looking at and what they cannot take from it. Most winner parts tables begin with no scope at all.
notes.excerpt_note: Cornell qualifies its own priced table in the same place: these prices are for one variant, and another would be cheaper.

notes.anchor: Green LED | — | 12
notes.title: A reader cannot buy these LEDs
notes.body: Both LED rows are blank in every column, and these are the parts the instrument is built around. The package, the forward voltage and whether they carry a built-in resistor would make them buyable without any price. That last one matters, because 4.2 drove them at 5 V and the table lists no resistors, so a reader cannot tell whether to add one. The Screws and Heat-set inserts rows have no quantity either, and 5.4 says four screws.
notes.after: | Green LED | [5 mm through-hole, forward voltage, internal resistor yes or no] | 12
notes.ballot: Is the documentation of the hardware system sufficient to enable reproduction by other teams?

notes.anchor: Bambu Lab PLA Basic, 1.75 mm, 1 kg spool
notes.title: The spool price is not the array's cost
notes.body: This is the only price on the page and it buys a whole kilogram of filament, where the array used six prints. Table 5's Filament (g) column is empty, and your slicer reported those six numbers when you printed the parts. Fill them in and the filament cost of one array falls out of the spool price you already have.
notes.after: | Filament, PLA | Bambu Lab PLA Basic, 1.75 mm, 1 kg spool | [g used across the six prints] | [355.99 per kg]
notes.ballot: Is the documentation of the hardware system sufficient to enable reproduction by other teams?

notes.anchor: the printed sensor fixture used for LED matching
notes.title: A load bearing part in no list
notes.body: Every one of the 40 readings was taken in this printed fixture, and it is in none of your three part lists: not Table 5's six printed parts, not Figure 14, not the six STL downloads. The wire-management prints of 3.1 are missing from the same three lists. This line also names a lux meter with no make or model, and every number on the page came off it.
notes.after: Lux meter [make and model], 3D printer, soldering iron, calipers, and the printed sensor fixture used for LED matching (STL below).
notes.ballot: Is the documentation of the hardware system sufficient to enable reproduction by other teams?

notes.anchor: Until it is written, Figure 16 shows how the parts stack
notes.title: Your assembly guide is already written in pieces
notes.body: The sequence is on the page, scattered. The hero gives the five parts in order, 6.2's section cut gives the stack and the 18 mm pitch, 5.4 gives four screws into heat-set inserts, and 5.1 gives the sliders. Collect them as numbered steps against the photographs you already have. This is the ballot question that carries the most weight here, and it needs no new work.
notes.after: 1 Screw the four posts to the bottom plate. 2 Seat the perf board on the posts. 3 [solder the LED harness, in this order]. 4 Drop the LED holder into the top of the housing. 5 Pass the two sliders through the housing sides. 6 Stand the tube holder on the LED holder, every tube bore over an LED bore.
notes.excerpt_note: Cornell names the deliverable and itemises it: assembly, operation, precautions, and the differences between variants.
notes.ballot: Is the documentation of the hardware system sufficient to enable reproduction by other teams?

notes.anchor: The CAD files below are numbered as in Figure 14
notes.title: Say how another team may use these
notes.body: Six downloadable meshes and no line saying what somebody may do with them. None of our four hardware pages has one, where Aachen states CC BY 4.0 in its own page text. One sentence under this heading settles it, and a repository link beside it would carry the Arduino sketch too.
notes.after: The CAD files below are numbered as in Figure 14. They are STL meshes in millimetres, in the instrument's own coordinates, so they open already assembled. Files and code: [repository link], released under [licence].
notes.ballot: Is the documentation of the hardware system sufficient to enable reproduction by other teams?

notes.anchor: in the instrument's own coordinates, so they open already assembled
notes.title: Files that open where they belong
notes.body: Units and a shared origin, so the six meshes open already assembled, and the download list carries the same numbering as the exploded view and the section cut. Two of the five Best Hardware winners claim CAD files and link none. Yours are here, and a stranger can place them.
notes.excerpt_note: Evry makes replication a design constraint in its opening, then links no file. You did the quiet half that page skipped.

notes.anchor: The LPA is not a new idea
notes.title: Prior art named and the contribution bounded
notes.body: You say the pattern is not yours, name it, and then say exactly what you added: the dual-wavelength column layout, the matched LED selection, and an enclosure sized for your own tubes. Two of the five winners cite no prior hardware at all. This paragraph is the overgraduate register, and claiming less costs you nothing.
notes.excerpt_note: TUDarmstadt names the two prior DIY designs and then the gap they left. Same move, same effect.

notes.anchor: our LPA follows that pattern and is named after it
notes.title: The page never uses its own name
notes.body: This page calls the instrument the LPA throughout. Its URL and its nav entry call it DiOPAL, and our Digital Twin page says "Characterised on the DiOPAL plate apparatus". A judge arriving from the nav meets a page about a device with another name. Introduce both names once in Purpose, then use one of them everywhere.
notes.after: our DiOPAL follows that pattern and is named after it
notes.ballot: Is the documentation of the hardware system sufficient to enable reproduction by other teams?

notes.anchor: whose half‑maximal point is 4.66
notes.title: A references section with no references
notes.body: Two claims in this section rest on published work and neither names a paper. Our Math Model page has the citation for the second: Castillo-Hair, S. M. et al. (2019) Optogenetic control of Bacillus subtilis gene expression, Nature Communications 10:3099, with K-half at 4.66 plus or minus 0.63 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹. Your 4.66 agrees with it exactly, which is worth keeping. Copy the citation across and add one for the Light Plate Apparatus pattern.
notes.ballot: Is the documentation of the hardware system sufficient to enable reproduction by other teams?
